One council, three jobs

Event Planners in Moreton Bay

The City of Moreton Bay runs from the Redcliffe foreshore and Bribie Island across the growth corridors to farmland at Dayboro and Mount Mee. Those are three different events with three different supplier lists. Send the suburb, the date and the guest number, and planners covering that end of the council area can answer.

  • Three councils mergedCaboolture, Pine Rivers and Redcliffe were amalgamated into one local government area.
  • Water on three sidesRedcliffe is a peninsula with a long foreshore facing Moreton Bay.
  • Rail reaches the peninsulaRedcliffe is linked to Brisbane by the Houghton Highway and by rail.

One council area, from a bay foreshore to a working paddock.

Nothing else about planning here matters as much as which end you are at. The peninsula has services, permits and a sea breeze. The country west has space, and nothing else.

The City of Moreton Bay was formed by merging the old Caboolture, Pine Rivers and Redcliffe councils, and the result is enormous. It takes in a peninsula with water on three sides, an island at Bribie, a chain of fast growing suburbs through North Lakes and Kallangur, and genuine farming country at Samford Valley, Dayboro and Mount Mee. Anyone comparing event planners in Moreton Bay should lead with the suburb rather than the council name, because the range inside it is the whole story.

The other useful fact is proximity. The council area sits immediately north of Brisbane, so city suppliers work here routinely and travel loadings are modest by Queensland standards. That holds until you get out past Dayboro, where the driveways narrow, the mains services stop and a marquee event becomes a build rather than a booking.

In and around Moreton Bay

What are you planning in Moreton Bay?

Three quite different local markets sit inside one council. The peninsula, the growth corridor and the rural west each ask a different first question of a planner.

Start with

Weddings

Two shapes dominate. A foreshore ceremony on the peninsula with a reception nearby, which is a permit and a wind conversation, or a property wedding out west at Samford Valley or Mount Mee, which is a generator, water and ground conditions conversation. Very little in between.

Find planners

Parties and milestones

The growth corridor through North Lakes, Mango Hill and Narangba is full of young families, so first birthdays, naming days and christening lunches are constant. New estate blocks are generous but the streets are narrow and the neighbours are close, which makes parking and a finish time the first two questions.

Find planners

Corporate events

Most corporate work here is local and daytime: training days, community forums, openings and end of year functions for businesses along the Bruce Highway corridor. Groups wanting a rural setting for a strategy day look west to Samford Valley, which puts catering and transport back into a modest budget.

Find planners

Engagement parties

Frequently held at a family home, and here that could mean a suburban block at Strathpine or ten acres at Mount Mee. The difference decides everything downstream: a suburban engagement is a noise and parking job, a rural one is a power and lighting job.

Find planners

Proposals

The Redcliffe foreshore is the obvious setting and it faces east, so sunrise over the bay is the strong option rather than sunset. Bribie Island gives you the same light with fewer people on the sand. Check the tide, because a wide foreshore at low water is a long walk to the edge.

Find planners

Private celebrations

Wakes, anniversaries and retirement lunches stay close to home here, and the peninsula carries a large share of them because it has long been a retirement area. Venues with parking at the door matter more than a view when a quarter of the guests have mobility limits.

Planning support

How much help do you want in Moreton Bay?

The honest test here is whether the site supplies anything. A function room on the peninsula that owns its kitchen, bar and car park can run on coordination. Ten acres at Mount Mee cannot, at any budget.

A planner carries the whole build with you, from the first budget conversation to the last supplier leaving.

Usually engaged nine to fourteen months out.

Your plan is built. A coordinator takes it over in the final weeks and runs the day so you can be in it.

Venue sourcing

Planners who know a market can shortlist against your date, your numbers and your budget rather than sending you back to the same search results.

Event coordination

Coordination is the execution layer: suppliers confirmed, a run sheet everyone has, and one person answering questions on the day.

Wedding coordination

A wedding coordinator takes a plan you have already built and runs the day itself, so nobody in the wedding party is directing traffic.

Choosing well

Finding the right planner in Moreton Bay

Ask about the site before you ask about style. In a council area this large, the useful questions are all about what the address does or does not provide.

No. 01

Ask which end of the council they work

Coverage is rarely the whole city. A planner who runs events around Redcliffe and North Lakes may not have suppliers who will drive to Woodford or Mount Mee, and the difference is close to an hour. Ask for a recent example at your end of the council area, and ask which suppliers came with them.

No. 02

Get the foreshore permission settled early

Events on public foreshore land generally need a booking or permit from the council, with conditions on numbers, marquees, vehicles, amplified sound and alcohol. Apply before you print anything, because the good positions along the Redcliffe and Scarborough foreshore go early for the cool dry months. Budget for the fact that a foreshore reserve has no power and no kitchen.

No. 03

Ask what happens to the paddock after rain

Ground is the variable people forget on rural property events. A paddock that takes a truck in August will not take one after a wet week in February, and a bogged vehicle at bump in costs you the schedule. Ask what matting or hard standing the planner specifies, where vehicles park if the ground is soft, and who inspects the site in the week before.

No. 04

Check how guests get home from the peninsula

Redcliffe now has rail as well as the Houghton Highway, which changes what you can expect of guests who would rather not drive. Ask whether the last service works with your finish time, and whether the planner has a plan for people staying on the peninsula as against those heading back into Brisbane. A late finish and a 40 minute drive make that a real question.

One council name covers a foreshore, a housing estate and a cattle paddock. Quote the address, not the city.

On the ground

From the peninsula to the paddock

The council area holds about as much variety as any in the state. These three parts of it behave so differently that advice written for one of them will mislead you about the other two.

The peninsula has water and a permit process

Redcliffe sits on a peninsula with water on three sides and a long foreshore reserve running along it, from Woody Point up through Margate and Redcliffe to Scarborough. That is the reason people choose it and the reason it takes planning. Foreshore land is public, so an organised ceremony needs council approval, and the conditions usually cover numbers, marquees, vehicle access and amplified sound. The physical catch is wind. An exposed bay frontage moves light fabric, flowers and hair around in a way an inland lawn does not.

The growth corridor is newer than its infrastructure

North Lakes, Mango Hill, Kallangur, Burpengary and Narangba have added a great many homes in a short period, and the venues, the roads and the car parks have not kept up at the same rate. The practical effects are small but consistent. Function space books out further ahead than the size of the suburb suggests, a Saturday drive on the Bruce Highway corridor takes longer than a weekday estimate, and an at home party on a new estate street runs into parking before it runs into space.

West of the highway you are building a venue

Samford Valley, Dayboro, Mount Mee and Woodford are farming country, and a property event there supplies everything itself. There is no kitchen, no mains water for a caterer at scale, no bathrooms for 120 people and often no lighting past the house.

  • Size the generator for lighting, catering and sound together
  • Confirm potable water and where the caterer draws it
  • Check the driveway against a loaded truck, not a car
  • Nominate a wet weather structure, not a wet weather idea
  • Agree who walks the ground the week before

Questions

Planning an event in Moreton Bay

What does an event planner charge in Moreton Bay?

Site type moves the fee more than the suburb does. A function room on the peninsula that supplies its own kitchen, bar and car park is a defined piece of coordination work. A property event at Dayboro or Mount Mee adds site visits, generator and bathroom specification, a wet weather structure and a ground inspection, and the hours show up in the quote. Ask for a fee against the actual address rather than a starting figure.

Can we hold a ceremony on the Redcliffe foreshore?

Usually yes, with council approval, because the foreshore is public reserve rather than private land. Expect conditions on guest numbers, marquees, vehicle access, chairs, amplified sound and alcohol, and apply well before you set the date for a cool dry month. Plan for the wind as well as the paperwork. An exposed bay frontage will move light fabric and loose flowers, and there is no power or kitchen on a reserve.

Is a property wedding at Samford Valley or Mount Mee harder than a venue?

Yes, because on rural land you are supplying the venue rather than booking one. You set the layout, the guest number and the finish time, and in exchange you provide the power, the water, the bathrooms, the lighting, a structure for wet weather and somewhere on the grass for cars. Check what conditions the property carries before you commit, then check that a loaded truck and a coach can get in and turn around. Ground conditions after a wet week decide more than the forecast on the day.

Do guests need to drive to an event on the peninsula?

Not necessarily, since Redcliffe is connected to Brisbane by rail as well as by the Houghton Highway across the water. That gives you a genuine option for guests who would rather not drive home late, provided your finish time works with the last service. Check it before you set the run sheet. For anyone staying on the peninsula the walk home is short, which is worth saying on the invitation so people plan accordingly.

Will Brisbane suppliers travel into Moreton Bay?

Routinely, because the council area starts immediately north of the city and much of the population sits within about 40 minutes of it. Travel loadings are usually modest through Redcliffe, North Lakes and Strathpine. They stop being modest past Dayboro, Mount Mee and Woodford, where the drive is longer, the roads are slower and delivery plus collection is two round trips. Ask for delivery and collection priced separately so you can compare quotes properly.

Can we run an event on Bribie Island?

Yes, and unlike the bay islands further south it is reached by a bridge rather than a ferry, so suppliers drive on. What changes is distance and sand. Bribie sits at the northern end of the council area, so a city supplier is looking at a longer run than a Redcliffe job, and anything set on sand needs a hard standing plan for trestles, a bar and a dance floor. Confirm vehicle access to the site itself, not just to the island.
